The '''[[Sweden|Kingdom of Sweden]]''' has a moderately sized diplomatic network of 79 embassies and 9 consulates general, supplemented by honorary consulates, cultural centres and trade missions. In countries without Swedish representation, Swedish citizens can seek assistance from public officials in the foreign services of [[List of diplomatic missions of the Nordic countries|any of the other Nordic countries]], in accordance with the [[Helsinki Treaty]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 2011|title=Meld. St. 12 (2010–2011)|url=https://www.regjeringen.no/en/dokumenter/meld.-st.-12-20102011/id637527/sec3}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Treaty of Cooperation between Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden (the Helsinki Treaty)|url=https://norden.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:702145/FULLTEXT01.pdf|access-date=|website=|at=Article 34}}</ref>

Of note Sweden was the first Western country to have an embassy in [[Pyongyang]].<ref>{{cite web|title=About the Embassy|url=http://www.swedenabroad.com/Page____114015.aspx|publisher=Embassy of Sweden, Pyongyang|accessdate=19 August 2011}}</ref> The embassy in Pyongyang continues to provide limited consular services to citizens of several Western countries without a presence in [[North Korea]] and acts as the [[consular protecting power]] of the [[United States]], [[Canada]], and [[Australia]] since 1995.<ref>{{cite web|title=Om ambassaden|url=http://www.swedenabroad.com/Page____114017.aspx|publisher=Embassy of Sweden, Pyongyang|accessdate=19 August 2011|language=Swedish}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Foreign Relations: North Korea|url=http://answers.usa.gov/system/selfservice.controller?CONFIGURATION=1000&PARTITION_ID=1&CMD=VIEW_ARTICLE&ARTICLE_ID=10874&USERTYPE=1&LANGUAGE=en&COUNTRY=US|publisher=USA.gov|accessdate=19 August 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930073351/http://answers.usa.gov/system/selfservice.controller?CONFIGURATION=1000&PARTITION_ID=1&CMD=VIEW_ARTICLE&ARTICLE_ID=10874&USERTYPE=1&LANGUAGE=en&COUNTRY=US|archivedate=30 September 2011}}</ref>

==History==
Through the 19th century and the early years of the 20th century, most Swedish diplomatic missions were [[legation]]s. The [[ambassador]] question was dealt with in the council on 25 August 1947. It was decided that some Swedish legations would be elevated to embassies. The first Swedish legations to be elevated to embassies were those in [[Embassy of Sweden, Washington, D.C.|Washington, D.C.]], [[Embassy of Sweden, London|London]], [[Embassy of Sweden, Paris|Paris]], [[Embassy of Sweden, Moscow|Moscow]], [[Embassy of Sweden, Beijing|Nanjing]], [[Embassy of Sweden, Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] and [[Embassy of Sweden, Oslo|Oslo]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.svd.se/arkiv/1947-08-26/SVNY/3 |newspaper=[[Svenska Dagbladet]] |title=Principbeslut om ambassader |trans-title=Decision in principle on embassies |page=3 |date=26 August 1947 |access-date=23 July 2024 |language=sv |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In January 2010, the [[Swedish Foreign Ministry]] announced that its embassies in [[Bratislava]] ([[Slovakia]]), [[Dakar]] ([[Senegal]]), [[Dublin]] ([[Ireland]]), [[Ljubljana]] ([[Slovenia]]), [[Luxembourg City|Luxembourg]] ([[Luxembourg]]), and [[Sofia]] ([[Bulgaria]]) would be closed down, while existing section offices in [[Pristina]], [[Tbilisi]], [[Chișinău]], [[Tirana]], [[Bamako]], [[Ouagadougou]], [[Monrovia]], [[Kigali]], [[La Paz]], and [[Phnom Penh]] would be upgraded to embassies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.balkans.com/open-news.php?uniquenumber=56577|title=Sweden to open embassy in Tirana Albania |date=7 May 2010 |publisher=Balkans.com|access-date=27 May 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110204032120/http://www.balkans.com/open-news.php?uniquenumber=56577|archive-date=4 February 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In December 2010, it was announced by the Swedish Foreign Ministry that an additional five embassies would close down; the embassies affected were the ones in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]], [[Buenos Aires]], [[Argentina]], [[Hanoi]], [[Vietnam]], [[Kuala Lumpur]], [[Malaysia]] and [[Luanda]], [[Angola]].<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.regeringen.se/sb/d/13798/a/158228|title=Sverige stänger fem ambassader|date=22 December 2010|publisher=[[Ministry for Foreign Affairs (Sweden)|Ministry for Foreign Affairs]] |accessdate=27 December 2010|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101225135023/http://www.regeringen.se/sb/d/13798/a/158228|archivedate=25 December 2010}}</ref>

In August 2011, an agreement between the [[Swedish Social Democratic Workers' Party|Social Democrats]] and the [[Reinfeldt Cabinet|governing Reinfeldt Cabinet]] was announced, with the purpose of keeping the embassies in [[Argentina]], [[Vietnam]], [[Malaysia]] and [[Angola]] open.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dn.se/nyheter/sverige/s-backar--ambassader-raddas |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807021543/http://www.dn.se/nyheter/sverige/s-backar--ambassader-raddas |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 August 2011 |title= S backar – ambassader räddas |date=1 August 2011 |newspaper=[[Dagens Nyheter]] |accessdate=6 August 2011 |language=sv}}</ref>

On 30 August 2012, Sweden closed its embassy in [[Minsk]], with the Estonian Embassy charged with representing Swedish interests in [[Belarus]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.swedenabroad.com/sv-SE/Ambassader/Minsk/Aktuellt/Nyheter/Svenska-ambassaden-stangd-for-allmanheten-sys|title=Ambassaden inte öppen för allmänheten {{!}} SwedenAbroad|website=www.swedenabroad.com|language=sv-SE|access-date=2017-07-19}}</ref>

On 2 November 2016, the embassy in [[Lima]], [[Peru]], was re-opened.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.swedenabroad.com/es-ES/Embassies/Lima/|title=Lima {{!}} SwedenAbroad|website=www.swedenabroad.com|access-date=2016-12-14}}</ref> Six days later, on 8 November the embassy in [[Manila]], [[Philippines]], was re-opened, eight years after it was closed down.

In November 2021 the Swedish government announced that it would re-open embassies in [[Dublin]] and [[Brussels]], and open a consulate-general in [[San Francisco]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.government.se/press-releases/2021/11/government-intends-to-open-embassy-in-dublin-and-consulate-general-in-san-francisco/ | title=Government intends to open embassy in Dublin and consulate-general in San Francisco | date=3 November 2021 }}</ref> In November 2022, the [[Embassy of Sweden, Luanda|embassy in Luanda]] closed and in the same year the [[Embassy of Sweden, Lima|embassy in Lima]], which had reopened in 2016, also closed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.swedenabroad.se/sv/utlandsmyndigheter/angola-luanda/ |publisher=Embassy of Sweden, Luanda |title=Sveriges ambassad i Luanda stänger i november 2022 |trans-title=Sweden's embassy in Luanda will close in November 2022 |date=28 October 2022 |access-date=4 November 2022 |language=sv}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.swedenabroad.se/sv/om-utlandet-f%C3%B6r-svenska-medborgare/peru/reseinformation/nyheter/f%C3%B6r%C3%A4ndring-av-konsul%C3%A4r-hantering-i-lima/ |publisher=Sweden Abroad |title=Förändring av konsulär hantering i Lima |trans-title=Change of consular handling in Lima |date=21 April 2022 |access-date=29 March 2023 |language=sv}}</ref>

On 20 June 2024, the Swedish government decided that the embassies in Bamako and Ouagadougou would be closed. For continued effective engagement in the [[Sahel]] and [[West Africa]], the government also decided to initiate a process to reopen the embassy in Dakar. The closing is expected to be completed by the end of 2024, while the embassy in Dakar is expected to open in 2025.<ref name="Bamako and Ouagadougou (2024)">{{cite press release |url=https://www.regeringen.se/pressmeddelanden/2024/06/sveriges-ambassader-i-bamako-och-ouagadougou-avvecklas-och-en-ny-ambassad-i-dakar-planeras-att-etableras/ |publisher=[[Ministry for Foreign Affairs (Sweden)|Ministry for Foreign Affairs]] |title=Sveriges ambassader i Bamako och Ouagadougou avvecklas och en ny ambassad i Dakar planeras att etableras |trans-title=Sweden's embassies in Bamako and Ouagadougou are being closed, and a new embassy is planned to be established in Dakar |date=20 June 2024 |access-date=1 July 2024 |language=sv}}</ref>

The Swedish government announced in February 2025 that it intends to reopen the consulate-general in [[Houston]], United States, and elevate the consulate-general in Brussels to an embassy.<ref name="Regeringen-130225">{{cite press release |url=https://www.regeringen.se/pressmeddelanden/2025/02/sverige-starker-sin-diplomatiska-narvaro-i-belgien-och-usa/ |publisher=[[Ministry for Foreign Affairs (Sweden)|Ministry for Foreign Affairs]] |title=Sverige stärker sin diplomatiska närvaro i Belgien och USA |trans-title=Sweden strengthens its diplomatic presence in Belgium and the USA |date=13 February 2025 |access-date=17 February 2025 |language=sv}}</ref> In December 2025, the Swedish government decided to reopen a Swedish embassy in Lima in the fall of 2026.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.regeringen.se/pressmeddelanden/2025/12/sverige-oppnar-ambassad-i-peru/ |publisher=[[Ministry for Foreign Affairs (Sweden)|Ministry for Foreign Affairs]] |title=Sverige öppnar ambassad i Peru |trans-title=Sweden opens embassy in Peru |date=8 December 2025 |access-date=20 July 2026 |language=sv}}</ref>

extract:
The Kingdom of Sweden has a moderately sized diplomatic network of 79 embassies and 9 consulates general, supplemented by honorary consulates, cultural centres and trade missions. In countries without Swedish representation, Swedish citizens can seek assistance from public officials in the foreign services of any of the other Nordic countries, in accordance with the Helsinki Treaty.
Of note Sweden was the first Western country to have an embassy in Pyongyang. The embassy in Pyongyang continues to provide limited consular services to citizens of several Western countries without a presence in North Korea and acts as the consular protecting power of the United States, Canada, and Australia since 1995.
